questions.prompt: One single-threaded executor runs a 4 ms control timer (period 20 ms) and a subscription callback that can take 30 ms. What can happen to the control timer?
options: It is dropped permanently after the first period that it misses in the executor queue
Nothing: timers always preempt a running subscription callback in the executor thread
Its callbacks can start up to about 30 ms late, since the long callback cannot be preempted
It runs faster, because the executor batches the pending callbacks into one call
questions.explanation: Callbacks run to completion on one thread, so the timer waits behind the long callback.

questions.prompt: Three periodic tasks (C,T) in ms: (2,8), (3,12), (4,16). Give the total utilization U as a decimal (precision 0.001).
Rate-monotonic fixed priorities, preemptive: tasks (C,T) = (1,3), (1,5), (2,10) ms in priority order. Give the response time of the third task in ms (precision 0.01).

Chain: camera period 50 ms with 10 ms capture delay (periodic stage); detector event-driven with worst response 20 ms; controller timer period 10 ms with response 3 ms. Using the bound sum of (period if periodic + response), give the maximum data age in ms (precision 0.5).
A consumer needs 50 ms per message, the producer sends one every 33 ms, and the subscription uses KEEP_LAST with depth 50. What does the consumer see in steady state?
options: Messages that are roughly 2.5 s old, with no error reported
Messages about 33 ms old, because the producer rate sets the age
Always the newest message, because KEEP_LAST history keeps the latest one
An exception when the queue becomes full, so the fault is reported
questions.explanation: The queue stays full; each message waits about 50 x 50 ms = 2.5 s. Old data is dropped silently once full.

questions.prompt: A stale-data gate computes `now - stamp <= max_age`. The stamp comes from another computer whose clock is 2 s ahead, max_age is 0.2 s. What is wrong?
options: The gate will stop the robot constantly, since every single sample looks too old to use
The age is negative, so old data passes; require 0 <= age and fix the clock domain
The gate should compare the stamp against max_age directly, rather than comparing the age
Nothing is wrong: a smaller or even negative age is always the safe case for the gate
questions.explanation: Negative age passes the one-sided test even though the stamp is not trustworthy.

questions.prompt: Design: a vision detector (30 Hz, up to 40 ms) feeds a 100 Hz velocity controller. Describe how data crosses from the detector to the controller and what the controller does if the detector stalls.
rubric: Latest-wins hand-off (depth 1) carrying a capture stamp; the controller never blocks on the detector.
Age check against a max_age chosen from the latency bound plus margin, accepting only 0 <= age <= max_age.
Declared fallback on stale input (hold, decay to zero or stop) and a log/alert of the stall.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
